title: Natural Hom comparison on an ordinary étale factored chart
statement: Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Let $f:X\to Y$, $s:U\hookrightarrow X$, $v:V\hookrightarrow Y$, $i:U\hookrightarrow P$ and $p:P\to V$ be morphisms between Noetherian schemes, with $s,v$ open, $i$ closed and $fs=vpi$. Suppose all the displayed morphisms and their composites are separated of finite type and admit compactifications. Work in the ordinary unbounded étale module-sheaf derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with compact supports of [def-amb-etale-compact-support] and right adjoints $f^\times,p^\times,i^\times$ of [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. For every $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ set $B=i^\times p^\times v^*K$. For every bounded-below $H\in D(U_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ there are bijections, natural in $H$ and $K$, $$\operatorname{Hom}(H,B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(H,s^*f^\times K).$$ They are the inverse of the chain $$\operatorname{Hom}(H,s^*f^\times K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(s_!H,f^\times K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_!s_!H,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(v_!Rp_!i_*H,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Rp_!i_*H,v^*K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(H,B),$$ using the ordinary adjunction bijections and compact-support composition on bounded-below inputs. Neither $B$ nor $s^*f^\times K$ is assumed bounded below.

proof.text: Normalize the immersion factors first. For an open $w$ equal to $s$ or $v$, the compactification $(w,\mathrm{id})$ in [def-amb-etale-compact-support] computes $Rw_!=Dw_!$: direct image by the identity is the identity, including on a K-injective representative. For $i$, which is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], use $(\mathrm{id},i)$ to compute $Ri_!=Ri_*$. The closed immersion is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite], so [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact] gives exactness and $Ri_*H=i_*H$ for bounded-below $H$. Although that node is stated for abelian sheaves, it applies to the underlying abelian sheaves of a short exact sequence of $A$-module sheaves: direct image is the same section functor with its $A$-action, and kernels and cokernels have the underlying abelian kernels and cokernels. Thus $i_*$ is exact also with these coefficients. Exactness gives $\mathcal H^q(i_*H)=i_*\mathcal H^q(H)$ and, by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact], $\mathcal H^q(s_!H)=s_!\mathcal H^q(H)$, so both inputs remain bounded below. The natural comparisons of [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] transport these computations to the chosen compactifications; their domains are bounded-below inputs, which is all that is used here.

source.place: Tags 0F7I (lemma-shriek-well-defined), 0F51 (lemma-proper-f-shriek); open normalization by (w,id). Closed exactness: etale-cohomology.tex Tag 04FX; extension exactness: Tag 03S5.

proof.text: The open immersion $s$ is étale [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale] and, being displayed, separated of finite type by hypothesis. By [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] the termwise derived étale sum extension $Ds_{\Sigma!}$ is left adjoint to $s^*$ on the whole unbounded ordinary categories $D(-_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. By [lem-cbc-open-extension-zero-etale-adjunction-agreement] the natural isomorphism $\kappa:s_!\xrightarrow{\sim}s^{\mathrm{et}}_!$ of exact sheaf functors identifies the extension-by-zero adjunction $s_!\dashv s^{-1}$ with the sum-extension adjunction; applied degreewise, $\kappa$ is an isomorphism $Ds_!\cong Ds_{\Sigma!}$ of the induced derived functors, and precomposing the derived transposes with $\kappa$ gives the derived adjunction $Ds_!\dashv s^*$, with no boundedness condition. Apply it in its inverse Hom direction, followed by the inverse Hom direction of $Rf_!\dashv f^\times$ from [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. This gives natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(H,s^*f^\times K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(s_!H,f^\times K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_!s_!H,K)$. The latter adjunction applies because the given compactification is between Noetherian schemes. Both permit the arbitrary object $K$ in the statement.

source.place: Opening and final paragraphs: open locality of adjunctions; formal Hom adjunction expansion.

proof.text: Write $\alpha_{b,a}:Rb_!Ra_!\xrightarrow{\sim}R(ba)_!$ for the natural compositor of [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]. Apply it to $(s,f)$, $(i,p)$ and $(pi,v)$. All these morphisms and composites have exactly the compactifiability, separated finite-type, Noetherian and finite-ring hypotheses required by that node. Starting with the bounded-below $H$, its values and the intermediate compact-support values are bounded below, since that node works on $D^+$. After the normalizations in step 1, the equality $fs=vpi$ gives the isomorphism $\gamma_H:Rf_!s_!H\xrightarrow{\sim}v_!Rp_!i_*H$, namely $\gamma_H=(\alpha_{v,pi,H}\circ v_!(\alpha_{p,i,H}))^{-1}\circ\alpha_{f,s,H}$ with transport along the displayed equality understood. Precomposition by $\gamma_H^{-1}$ gives $\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_!s_!H,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(v_!Rp_!i_*H,K)$. Its inverse is precomposition by $\gamma_H$. This uses composition only on bounded-below inputs; precomposition makes sense for every target $K$.

source.place: Tag 0F7J, lemma-shriek-composition; Tag 0F7K, lemma-pseudo-functor (coherent choice of the compositors).

proof.text: Put $T=Rp_!i_*H$. The open immersion $v$ is étale [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale] and separated of finite type by hypothesis, so, exactly as in step 2, [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] and the adjunction identification of [lem-cbc-open-extension-zero-etale-adjunction-agreement] give the unbounded ordinary derived adjunction $Dv_!\dashv v^*$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(v_!T,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(T,v^*K)$, natural in $T$ and $K$. Substitution of the functorial value $T$ preserves naturality in $H$. This ambient adjunction imposes no bounded-below condition on $K$.

source.place: Final paragraph: open locality of adjunctions, expanded at v.

proof.text: Apply [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] to $p$ and $i$, whose compactifications and Noetherian hypotheses are assumed. The Hom bijections for $Rp_!\dashv p^\times$ and $Ri_!\dashv i^\times$, together with $Ri_!H\cong i_*H$ from step 1, give $\operatorname{Hom}(Rp_!i_*H,v^*K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(i_*H,p^\times v^*K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(H,i^\times p^\times v^*K)$. These are the ambient adjunctions, so the input $p^\times v^*K$ for the last adjunction need not be bounded below. Their naturality holds for all morphisms of $K$ and of bounded-below $H$.

source.place: Opening and final paragraphs: closed/projection factorization and composition of adjunctions.

proof.text: Compose the bijections of steps 2 through 5 to obtain $\Theta_{H,K}:\operatorname{Hom}(H,s^*f^\times K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(H,B)$. Define the asserted comparison to be $\Theta_{H,K}^{-1}$, the reverse composite of those same bijections. Each Hom adjunction commutes with precomposition in its source and postcomposition in its target. For step 3, naturality is exactly $\gamma_H\circ Rf_!s_!(a)=(v_!Rp_!i_*)(a)\circ\gamma_{H\prime}$ for $a:H\prime\to H$, and associativity of composition handles postcomposition by any $K\to K\prime$. Substituting these equalities consecutively proves naturality of $\Theta$. Inverting a commuting square of bijections proves naturality of its inverse. The two inverse identities are obtained by cancelling each adjacent bijection with its inverse. Hence the comparison is precisely the inverse of the chain in the statement, with neither representing target required to lie in $D^+$.

lean.note: Canonical helpers belong to this comparison: open and closed compact-support normalizations, the D+ left comparison and its ambient value, and the explicit forward Hom chain. The theorem supplies its inverse, natural in both variables, for arbitrary chosen ambient right adjoints F, G, I with their adjunctions. No boundedness assumption is placed on K or either representing target; only H belongs to the full D+ subcategory. All helper data are constructed from existing canonical comparisons, with no choice of an unspecified isomorphism.
